name: Red Flags When Hiring a Bathroom Overhauling Contractor in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What early red flags should I watch for when interviewing bathroom overhauling contractors in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What early red flags should I watch for when interviewing bathroom overhauling contractors in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Spotting red flags early can save you from major stress during a bathroom overhaul. Be cautious of contractors who provide only vague, one-line estimates without detailed scope or materials, or who resist putting verbal promises in writing. Pressure for large cash deposits, especially before any design, permit, or ordering work begins, is another concern. Verify licensing and insurance; if a contractor cannot promptly provide license numbers or proof of current liability and workers’ compensation coverage, reconsider. A lack of recent local references for similar bathroom overhauls, or reluctance to share project photos and addresses, suggests limited relevant experience. Pay attention to how they discuss permits, inspections, and waterproofing. Dismissing permits as unnecessary, promising to “work around” code, or brushing off waterproofing questions are major warning signs. Reliable contractors should be comfortable explaining inspection stages, typical timelines, and how they ensure showers are properly waterproofed. Observe their professionalism before you hire them: missed or repeatedly rescheduled appointments, chronic lateness without explanation, and poor communication during bidding often foreshadow problems once work starts. Trust your instincts; if you feel rushed, talked over, or ignored when you ask detailed questions, keep interviewing other contractors until you find one who is transparent and respectful.
acceptedAnswer.description: Watch for vague or handwritten estimates, reluctance to put promises in writing, pressure for large cash deposits, no verifiable license or insurance, no recent local references, and dismissive answers about permits, waterproofing, and inspections. Multiple missed or late appointments before hiring are also warning signs.
